question: Do plants with a documented traditional antidiabetic use yield natural products with higher model-predicted PTP1B activity than Duke-covered control plants without such a use?
motivation: Ethnopharmacology assumes traditional use enriches for bioactivity. This assumption is rarely tested quantitatively at scale. The PhytoTruth PTP1B model never observes ethnobotanical data, so traditional-use status is an independent label.

prior_inspection_disclosure.statement: Full disclosure of what was examined before this protocol was frozen. A feasibility gate was run on 2026-11-06 to decide whether the data sources could be joined at all.
what_was_inspected: Counts of Duke ETHNOBOT records, unique taxa, and antidiabetic taxa.
Overlap counts between NPASS species names and Duke taxa.
Resolution rate of the 101 existing PTP1B screening candidates to source plants.
A candidate-level overlap statistic: 5/71 Duke-covered candidate plants carried an antidiabetic use versus 115/3480 background (2.13x, Fisher one-sided p=0.0903).
prior_inspection_disclosure.why_that_does_not_invalidate_this_protoc: The primary outcome specified below is plant-level median predicted pChEMBL over NPASS compounds. No predicted activity value, no plant-level score, and no group comparison of model output was computed or inspected before freezing. The inspected candidate-overlap statistic is a different estimand on a different population (101 pre-ranked candidates, not the Duke-covered NPASS population) and is reported here as exploratory context only, never as a confirmatory result.

duke_ethnobotany.provides: plant TAXON to traditional ACTIVITY records with references

data_sources.model: experiments/ml_activity_chembl335 (frozen; not refitted, retuned, or recalibrated by this phase)

population.inclusion: NPASS source organism whose normalized species_name matches a Duke ETHNOBOT TAXON exactly after normalization, and which has at least `min_compounds_per_plant` NPASS compounds with a parsable structure.
population.rationale_for_conditioning_on_duke_cover: Only plants Duke covers can be labelled. Including Duke-absent plants would confound traditional-use status with database coverage.

group_assignment.case: At least one ETHNOBOT record whose ACTIVITY matches any of the diabetes terms below.

negative_control.purpose: Guard against the confound that well-studied plants have more compounds and more recorded uses of every kind.
negative_control.design: Repeat the identical comparison using a traditional-use category with no expected PTP1B relevance.
negative_control.interpretation_rule: If the negative-control comparison is as large as the diabetes comparison, the primary result is attributed to study bias, not to pharmacological convergence, and must be reported as such.

scoring.model_output: predicted pChEMBL from the frozen PTP1B XGBoost artifact
scoring.sampling: If a plant exceeds the cap, draw a uniform random sample without replacement using the fixed seed. Caps bound compute and prevent heavily sampled plants from dominating.

primary_outcome.comparison: traditional antidiabetic plants versus Duke-covered control plants
primary_outcome.test: two-sided Mann-Whitney U at the plant level
primary_outcome.effect_size: rank-biserial correlation and Hodges-Lehmann median shift

uncertainty.clustering: Plants within the same botanical family are not independent. Report a family-clustered bootstrap 95% CI for the median shift, resampling families with replacement.

declare_convergence_supported_only_if: family-clustered bootstrap 95% CI for the median shift excludes 0
the negative-control median shift is smaller than the primary median shift
support_rule.if_any_condition_fails: Report as NOT SUPPORTED. Do not reframe a secondary analysis as the primary outcome. Do not drop the negative control.

sensitivity_analyses: Restrict to compounds inside the model applicability domain.
Use per-plant mean and per-plant 90th percentile instead of the median.
Exclude plants contributing more than one genus-level duplicate.
declared_limitations: Predicted activity is not measured activity. This tests convergence with a model, not experimental confirmation.
Duke coverage is biased toward well-studied and temperate/North American floras.
Traditional 'antidiabetic' use is recorded against a modern disease label applied retrospectively to heterogeneous historical sources.
NPASS compound-organism edges are reported provenance, not independently verified occurrence.
A single target (PTP1B) cannot represent antidiabetic activity in general.
Exact species-name matching misses synonyms and will undercount true overlap.
This analysis does not and cannot establish efficacy or safety of any plant or preparation.

traditional_knowledge_handling.attribution: Every traditional-use claim retains its Duke REFERENCE and COUNTRY fields in the output tables.
traditional_knowledge_handling.framing: Convergence evidence only. The analysis must never state that traditional knowledge is validated or invalidated by a model prediction.
traditional_knowledge_handling.nagoya_note: No genetic resources are accessed. Only published literature records are used.
